[ 1 ]  His father was Crown Prince Wilhelm , the eldest son and heir to the German Emperor, Wilhelm II . His mother was Duchess Cecilie of Mecklenburg-Schwerin . The former Crown Prince and his family remained in Potsdam , where Wilhelm and his younger brothers attended the local gymnasium .

Ernest Augustus was deprived of the throne of Hanover upon its annexation by Prussia in 1866 and later the Duchy of Brunswick in 1884. Ernest Augustus was deprived of his British peerages and honours for having sided with Germany in World War I .

 When King George V died in Paris on 12 June 1878, Prince Ernest Augustus succeeded him as Duke of Cumberland and Teviotdale in the Peerage of Great Britain and Earl of Armagh in the Peerage of Ireland . Queen Victoria created him a Knight of the Garter on 20 July 1878. Emperor Franz Joseph I of Austria appointed him to succeed his father as colonel and proprietor of the Austrian 42nd Regiment of Infantry. The regiment's name was changed to honour him, and he served as its honorary colonel from 1879 to the fall of the Austro-Hungarian Empire, in 1918.

On 24 October 1913, he renounced his succession rights to the Brunswick duchy (which had belonged to the Guelph dynasty since 1235) in favour of his son. The younger Ernest Augustus thus became the reigning Duke of Brunswick on 1 November 1913 and married the Kaiser's daughter. Princess Maria Alix of Saxony (1901–1990), wife of Prince Franz Joseph of Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen, photographed with her two-year-old son, Prince Karl Anton (1922–1993), in a charming portrait.

Born at Wachwitz, near Dresden, on 27 September 1901, Maria Alix was a daughter of King Friedrich August III, the last reigning King of Saxony, and Archduchess Luise of Austria-Tuscany.

On 25 May 1921, she married Prince Franz Joseph of Hohenzollern (1891–1964) at Schloss Sibyllenort in Silesia. Remarkably, her elder sister, Princess Margarete, had married Franz Joseph’s twin brother, Hereditary Prince Friedrich Viktor, the previous year.

Their son, Prince Karl Anton, was born in Munich on 28 January 1922. He later married Alexandrine Afif in Rome on 15 August 1951 and died at Hechingen on 3 November 1993.

Maria Alix and Franz Joseph subsequently welcomed three more children: Princes Meinrad and Emanuel Joseph, and Princess Maria Margarethe.

Through her marriage, Maria Alix became a member of the Hohenzollern princely family, whose close dynastic connections included the royal houses of Romania, Portugal, and the Two Sicilies.

In this affectionate portrait, the young princess, wearing an elegantly patterned gown, sits with her little son upon her lap. Their relaxed pose offers a delightful glimpse of motherhood within one of Germany’s former ruling families.
